# Time Loop

Build **Time Loop**, a 30-second time loop platformer where past-self replays
help solve puzzles in Godot 4 at `/workspace/game/`. This is not a prototype.
It is a **complete, shippable micro-game** that could sit on an itch.io page or
Steam as a polished vertical slice.

## Core Vision

Each level is a 30-second loop. When the timer expires, time rewinds and the
player starts again — but a ghost of the previous loop replays simultaneously,
interacting with the world. The ghost can hold switches, distract enemies, or
stand on pressure plates while the current player tackles other objectives.
Multiple loops layer: loop 1's ghost holds a door open, loop 2's ghost stands
on a platform to create a bridge, and in loop 3 the player finally reaches the
exit using both ghosts' contributions. The puzzle is temporal coordination —
planning what each loop-self needs to do and when, so that all versions
cooperate across time. Twenty-four levels across four chapters escalate from
single-ghost puzzles to four-loop orchestrations.

## What the Player Experiences

A title screen shows overlapping clock hands and ghost silhouettes. A chapter
menu reveals four chapters of six levels each.

Entering a level starts a 30-second countdown. The player runs, jumps, and
interacts with switches and objects. When the timer hits zero, the screen
flashes and rewinds — the player restarts at the spawn point, but a translucent
ghost replays exactly what they did in the previous loop. The ghost physically
interacts with the world: it presses buttons, holds doors, and blocks lasers.

The player can layer up to four loops. A timeline bar at the top shows all
active ghosts and their current positions in the 30-second window. Reaching the
exit crystal with all required switches held (by ghosts or player) completes
the level. A reset button clears all ghosts to start fresh. Level-complete
shows loops used and time of exit within the final loop.

## Assets

2D assets are mounted read-only at:

- `/workspace/assets/library/` — Kenney CC0 packs (sprites, tiles, UI, fonts).
- `/workspace/assets/library-oga/` — OpenGameArt entries; respect each
  subdir's `LICENSE.txt`.

Browse the library and choose packs.
Copy what you need into your project's `assets/` folder.

## Project layout

```
/workspace/game/
  project.godot
  Main.tscn
  demo_outputs/    <- your input traces (1-10 files)
  scripts/  scenes/  assets/
```

The build must launch cleanly with:

```
godot --headless --path /workspace/game --quit-after 5
```

A reference for Godot CLI flags is at `/workspace/tools/godot_command_line.md`.
**Engine flags like `--headless` and `--quit-after N` must come BEFORE `--`** —
anything after `--` is forwarded to the project as user args and silently
ignored by the engine. Correct shape:
`godot --headless --quit-after 5 --path . -- --scenario near_victory`.

A screenshot helper is available at `/workspace/tools/screenshot.sh`. Use it to actually see what your UI / battlefield /
result screens look like.

```
/workspace/tools/screenshot.sh --path /workspace/game \
      -- --out /workspace/frame.png --frames 60
```

To screenshot a specific scenario, append `--scenario <id>` after `--`. The
helper consumes only `--out` / `--frames` / `--scene`; remaining args stay in
`OS.get_cmdline_user_args()` for your game code to read. Example:

```
/workspace/tools/screenshot.sh --path /workspace/game \
      -- --out /workspace/battle_debug.png --frames 120 --scenario battle
```

## Demos

Ship **1-10 input-trace files** under `/workspace/game/demo_outputs/`, one per
demo, each named `*.json`. The evaluator launches a fresh game per trace,
replays your trace as synthetic mouse and keyboard input at 1280x720, and
records the screen. Only the first 10 traces by filename are evaluated;
recordings longer than 20 s are sampled from a random 20 s window.

### Scenarios

Normal play should start from the title screen and demonstrate the task's
core gameplay loop.
Demo playback must be deterministic. For demos that need a specific state
(a specific level, combat state, upgrade screen, result state, or late-game
setup), define named scenarios your game loads when launched with:

```
godot --path /workspace/game -- --scenario <id>
```

When `--scenario <id>` is present the game must skip menus, set up the named
state deterministically (seed any RNG), and begin accepting input immediately.

### Trace file format

```json
{
  "scenario": "title_flow",
  "duration_frames": 360,
  "events": [
    {"frame": 30,  "type": "mouse_click", "button": "left", "x": 300, "y": 360},
    {"frame": 90,  "type": "key_press",   "keycode": "1"},
    {"frame": 180, "type": "key_press",   "keycode": "SPACE"},
    {"frame": 300, "type": "wait"}
  ]
}
```

- `scenario` — optional; omit for a normal game launch from the title screen.
- `duration_frames` — total frames to record at 30 fps; cap at **600 (20 s)**.
- `events` — time-ordered inputs. Coordinates are pixels in the 1280x720
  viewport. Supported types:
  - `mouse_click`: `{frame, type, button: "left"|"right", x, y}`
  - `mouse_down` / `mouse_up`: `{frame, type, button: "left"|"right", x, y}` —
    use these for drag interactions: emit `mouse_down` at the start point,
    one or more `mouse_move` events along the way, and `mouse_up` at the end.
    A `mouse_click` is a `mouse_down` + `mouse_up` at the same point in tight
    succession.
  - `mouse_move`: `{frame, type, x, y}`
  - `key_press` / `key_down` / `key_up`: `{frame, type, keycode}` — keycodes:
    `A`-`Z`, `0`-`9`, `ESCAPE`, `ENTER`, `SPACE`, `TAB`, `BACKSPACE`,
    `DELETE`, `SHIFT`, `CTRL`, `ALT`, `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`.
  - `wait`: `{frame, type}` — anchor frame, no input.

Replay must be deterministic: same trace, fresh launch, same outcome every time.

`godot --headless --quit-after 5 --path . -- --scenario near_victory`.

A screenshot helper is available at `/workspace/tools/screenshot.sh`. Use it to actually see what your UI / battlefield /
result screens look like.

```
/workspace/tools/screenshot.sh --path /workspace/game \
      -- --out /workspace/frame.png --frames 60
```

To screenshot a specific scenario, append `--scenario <id>` after `--`. The
helper consumes only `--out` / `--frames` / `--scene`; remaining args stay in
`OS.get_cmdline_user_args()` for your game code to read. Example:

```
/workspace/tools/screenshot.sh --path /workspace/game \
      -- --out /workspace/battle_debug.png --frames 120 --scenario battle
```

## Demos

Ship **1-10 input-trace files** under `/workspace/game/demo_outputs/`, one per
demo, each named `*.json`. The evaluator launches a fresh game per trace,
replays your trace as synthetic mouse and keyboard input at 1280x720, and
records the screen. Only the first 10 traces by filename are evaluated;
recordings longer than 20 s are sampled from a random 20 s window.

### Scenarios

Normal play should start from the title screen and demonstrate the task's
core gameplay loop.
Demo playback must be deterministic. For demos that need a specific state
(a specific level, combat state, upgrade screen, result state, or late-game
setup), define named scenarios your game loads when launched with:

```
godot --path /workspace/game -- --scenario <id>
```

When `--scenario <id>` is present the game must skip menus, set up the named
state deterministically (seed any RNG), and begin accepting input immediately.

### Trace file format

```json
{
  "scenario": "title_flow",
  "duration_frames": 360,
  "events": [
    {"frame": 30,  "type": "mouse_click", "button": "left", "x": 300, "y": 360},
    {"frame": 90,  "type": "key_press",   "keycode": "1"},
    {"frame": 180, "type": "key_press",   "keycode": "SPACE"},
    {"frame": 300, "type": "wait"}
  ]
}
```

- `scenario` — optional; omit for a normal game launch from the title screen.
- `duration_frames` — total frames to record at 30 fps; cap at **600 (20 s)**.
- `events` — time-ordered inputs. Coordinates are pixels in the 1280x720
  viewport. Supported types:
  - `mouse_click`: `{frame, type, button: "left"|"right", x, y}`
  - `mouse_down` / `mouse_up`: `{frame, type, button: "left"|"right", x, y}` —
    use these for drag interactions: emit `mouse_down` at the start point,
    one or more `mouse_move` events along the way, and `mouse_up` at the end.
    A `mouse_click` is a `mouse_down` + `mouse_up` at the same point in tight
    succession.
  - `mouse_move`: `{frame, type, x, y}`
  - `key_press` / `key_down` / `key_up`: `{frame, type, keycode}` — keycodes:
    `A`-`Z`, `0`-`9`, `ESCAPE`, `ENTER`, `SPACE`, `TAB`, `BACKSPACE`,
    `DELETE`, `SHIFT`, `CTRL`, `ALT`, `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`.
  - `wait`: `{frame, type}` — anchor frame, no input.

Replay must be deterministic: same trace, fresh launch, same outcome every time.

sections.content: Objective: reach the exit crystal while all required switches are held by the live player or replay ghosts. Core loop: enter a level, run and jump, activate switches or objects, let the 30-second timer expire when needed, then cooperate with the new ghost replay of the previous loop. Success: exit crystal with all required switches held; level-complete shows loops used and exit time. Failure or retry: timer expiry is not a terminal failure; it rewinds and adds or reuses ghost layers. Reset clears ghosts and restarts fresh. Puzzle verb: temporal coordination across layered loops, including switches, pressure plates, buttons, doors, lasers, and enemy distraction.

Menu controls: mouse click selects title, chapter, level, reset, and level-complete buttons. Play controls: LEFT and RIGHT or A and D move; SPACE jumps; ENTER interacts with nearby switches or objects; R activates reset; ESCAPE toggles the assumed pause overlay. Trace-compatible keys only: A-Z, 0-9, ESCAPE, ENTER, SPACE, TAB, BACKSPACE, DELETE, SHIFT, CTRL, ALT, UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT. Mouse coordinates are in the 1280x720 viewport. The timeline bar is display-only. Drag interactions are not required, but if used traces must emit mouse_down, mouse_move, and mouse_up.

Normal flow: title screen -> chapter menu -> level select -> level play -> rewind loop or level complete -> return or replay. Scenario flow: with --scenario id, skip menus and load the named deterministic state. Loop flow: timer zero flashes, rewinds, respawns the live player, and replays the prior ghost. Reset flow: reset clears all ghosts and restarts the level fresh. Pause flow, assumed: ESC opens a pause overlay with resume, restart, and return to chapter; pausing does not change loop timing. Result flow: level-complete shows loops used and exit time, then returns to chapter or retries. No explicit death failure is required; loop expiry and reset provide retry.

Content is data-driven: 4 chapters x 6 levels = 24 levels. Chapter 1 introduces one-ghost switches and pressure plates. Chapter 2 introduces doors held open and bridges or platforms. Chapter 3 introduces lasers and enemy distraction. Chapter 4 uses four-loop orchestration. Level data includes id, chapter, index, spawn, exit crystal, required switches, max loops, ghost tracks, and deterministic seed. Numeric parameters: 30-second loop, 1280x720 demo viewport, 30 fps trace frames, 600-frame cap, and up to four loop timelines by default. Named scenarios: loop_rewrite_imminent starts near timer expiry with one ghost track; multi_ghost_door starts with two ghosts and a held door; laser_block_bridge starts with three ghosts near a laser or plate puzzle; four_loop_finale starts on the final loop with required switches held; result_state loads a level-complete summary deterministically. No upgrade screen or combat progression is included because it is not specified for this genre.

Title screen shows overlapping clock hands and ghost silhouettes with legible start or menu prompts. Chapter menu shows four chapters and six level slots with clear selection highlight. Level HUD shows countdown, timeline bar at top, reset button, and required-switch status. Timeline bar marks the 30-second window and each active ghost position without overlapping countdown text. Rewind uses a screen flash and ghost translucency. Switches, pressure plates, buttons, doors, lasers, enemy distraction triggers, and the exit crystal have active and inactive visual states aligned with their interaction bounds. Level-complete panel shows loops used and final-loop exit time with non-overlapping text at 1280x720. Screenshot helper captures can be used to verify title, play, and result readability.

Asset purposes: player and ghost sprites, tileset or platform collision visuals, clock hands and ghost silhouettes for title, UI font, buttons, panels, timeline icons, switch, pressure plate, button, door, laser, enemy or distraction marker, and exit crystal. Source: browse /workspace/assets/library Kenney CC0 packs and /workspace/assets/library-oga OpenGameArt entries, then copy needed files into game/assets. Respect each OpenGameArt subdir LICENSE.txt when copying. Fallback: if a specific library sprite is unavailable, use simple generated or placeholder 2D shapes while preserving copied-library obligations and license attribution. Do not treat read-only mounts as writable runtime storage.

Godot 4 project at /workspace/game with project.godot, Main.tscn, demo_outputs, scripts, scenes, and assets. Main.tscn hosts app flow and reads OS.get_cmdline_user_args for scenario and screenshot helper arguments. Proposed autoloads: GameManager for state and loop count, LevelManager for level data and chapter progression, InputRecorder for deterministic 30 Hz frames, GhostSystem for replay tracks, ScenarioLoader for named setups, and DeterministicRng with fixed seeds. Scenes: TitleScreen, ChapterMenu, LevelSelect, Level, Player, Ghost, Switch, PressurePlate, Button, Door, Laser, EnemyDistractor, ExitCrystal, HUD, TimelineBar, and LevelCompletePanel. Data: JSON or Resource files under assets define levels, ghost tracks, and scenarios. Simulation uses fixed 30 Hz gameplay ticks for trace alignment, with rendering decoupled. Headless launch must avoid blocking popups. Engine flags are placed before --; user args appear after --.

QA can validate without replay evidence as follows. 1. Inspect /workspace/game for required layout and run godot --headless --path /workspace/game --quit-after 5 (R020,R021). 2. Launch the normal title trace 00_title_core.json and observe title visuals, chapter menu, level entry, movement, switch interaction, and either completion or loop setup (R009,R010,R011,R026). 3. Launch scenario loop_rewrite_imminent with godot --path /workspace/game -- --scenario loop_rewrite_imminent and observe the near-expiry countdown, screen flash, respawn, and translucent ghost replay (R003,R004,R012,R014). 4. Launch scenario multi_ghost_door and observe layered ghosts holding a door or bridge while the live player advances (R006,R013,R014). 5. Launch scenario laser_block_bridge and observe ghost pressure plate, laser block, or enemy distraction (R005,R013). 6. Launch scenario four_loop_finale and observe required switches held by ghosts or player, exit crystal completion, and level-complete stats (R007,R008,R015,R017). 7. Launch scenario result_state to verify level-complete stats deterministically (R017). 8. Inspect demo_outputs for 1-10 JSON files, duration_frames <= 600, time-ordered events, and supported event or keycode shapes (R024,R030,R031,R032). 9. Re-run selected traces twice from fresh launches and compare observable screenshots or logs for deterministic outcome (R027,R033). 10. Inspect game/assets and license files to verify library copying and OpenGameArt license respect (R018,R019). Use /workspace/tools/screenshot.sh with --scenario where visual capture is needed (R034). This plan covers R001 through R034.

assumptions: Default keyboard bindings are LEFT and RIGHT for movement, SPACE for jump, ENTER for interact, R for reset, and ESCAPE for pause or back. Demos use only supported keycodes.
Pause is an assumed convenience rather than an instruction-mandated mechanic: ESC toggles a pause overlay with resume, restart, and return options while preserving the 30-second loop rules.
A loop is treated as one 30-second run. Default content uses up to four total loop iterations for four-loop orchestration, while the ghost system can be configured for scenario tooling.
Switches, pressure plates, buttons, doors, lasers, and enemy-distraction triggers are simple deterministic trigger or collision volumes.
Enemies can be distracted by ghost presence and serve as puzzle blockers or attention triggers; no enemy-combat progression or upgrade system is required.
There is no explicit death failure in the instruction. Timer expiry is a rewind, and reset provides a fresh retry state.
Deterministic replay uses a fixed 30 Hz gameplay tick aligned with trace frames; rendering may be decoupled from simulation.
Ghost recording stores per-frame input, transform, and trigger state needed to reproduce interactions without wall-clock dependence.
Level select may show all 24 levels for demonstration even if normal progression unlocks them sequentially.
The reset action is exposed both as an on-screen button and as the R key for trace convenience.
The timeline bar is display-only and does not require mouse interaction.
Named scenarios may preload scripted ghost tracks as if they were previously recorded so late-loop states can be demonstrated within the trace cap.
No audio requirements are specified; audio is optional and must not affect deterministic validation.
If a required library sprite is unavailable, simple generated or placeholder 2D shapes may be used while still copying chosen library assets and preserving license obligations.
content.change_summary: Initial grounded design for Time Loop. It defines requirements for the 30-second loop, ghost interaction, four-chapter content, menus, timeline HUD, reset and level-complete feedback, asset sourcing, project layout, headless launch, deterministic scenario playback, and trace format. Eight design sections operationalize the requirements with deterministic named scenarios for states that exceed the 20-second trace cap.

summaries: Initial Time Loop Godot 4 project implementation: title/chapter/level-select/HUD/pause/level-complete flow, fixed 30 Hz loop gameplay with player movement, rewind ghosts, pressure plates, levers, doors, lasers, enemy distraction, exit-crystal checks, reset, timeline bar, and deterministic named scenarios. All geometry and UI use the supplied normalized art package paths at runtime.

Repair the failed Godot import stage by removing eager preloads of the three large UI textures from scripts/main.gd. Replace them with lazy cached loads through helper getters so class registration and import scanning do not simultaneously load large PNG resources. This preserves all title, chapter, level, HUD, pause, scenario, reset, timeline, and level-complete flows while addressing the OOM-killed reimport step.

Fix the Godot 4.5 GDScript parse errors in scripts/level.gd by replacing unsupported sinf() calls with typed float sin() expressions. This unblocks compilation of the level script and its dependent main preload while preserving all existing loop, ghost, prop, scenario, HUD, reset, and completion behavior.

Replace all dynamic string-based Callable(self, "method") constructs in scripts/main.gd with statically analyzable lambdas. This preserves every title, chapter menu, level select, HUD reset, level-complete, and pause button behavior while removing the Tier 1 primitives that caused Godot MCP strict-mode launch to fail before any screenshot could be captured.

Repair chapter and level-select button callbacks so each loop iteration captures its own chapter/level identifier. This prevents a GDScript closure-capture edge case where all buttons could bind to the final loop value. The project retains the existing title, HUD, level, ghost, rewind, reset, pause, and scenario flow. This patch does not claim host import success; the previous import was killed by the sandbox before emitting a script error and must be re-run against this fresh source state.

decisions.summary: Correcting the rejected decision: the earlier evidence mapping cited the probe session, which is not a capture; it is withdrawn and all mappings below cite actual successful capture sessions and their real checkpoint frames. Four executed trials already cover ordinary title-to-chapter navigation, ordinary Quick Start play (movement, jump, reset, pause open), the loop_rewrite_imminent rewind/ghost boundary, and the result_state completion panel, and all eight fresh replays matched state and pixels. With the single remaining trial I target the last uncovered ordinary-menu criterion: the level-select screen that must reveal six level entries per chapter (R010/R008), using the observed Chapter Menu rect [500,340,280,70] and Chapter 1 rect [480,210,320,72], then attempting the first level entry at the same list position and capturing the outcome. Packaged demo replay remains impossible because no demo traces ship in the project; that gap is reported, not fabricated.

findings.description: Ordinary navigation works: a fresh title launch shows the TIME LOOP title (supplied pixels show overlapping clock hands and ghost silhouettes), and clicking the observed Chapter Menu rect opens a Chapters panel with exactly four chapter buttons plus Back (frame 30-119 observations and supplied frame_0119 pixels).
findings.uncertainty: The six-level-per-chapter level-select screen behind each chapter button has not been observed yet; the planned ordinary_level_select_probe trial targets it.

After one real click on the observed Chapter Menu rect, the Chapters panel lists Chapter 1-4 buttons plus Back, evidencing the four-chapter menu half of R010; six-level lists remain to be captured.

Level 1-1 HUD after ordinary Quick Start: Time 29.20 counting down from 30, Loop 1, Switches Held 0/1, timeline bar control rect [36,58,1204,30], and Reset button, evidencing countdown start, play HUD and timeline presence.

A replayed ghost stands on plate_1 making it active with Switches Held 1/1 while the live player idles at spawn, and two ghost sprites are visible in the supplied pixels, evidencing simultaneous ghost presence and physical plate holding.

decisions.summary: Trial budget exhausted; finishing with measured evidence. Five captured traces (ordinary title->chapter->level-select navigation, ordinary Quick Start play with movement/reset/pause, loop_rewrite_imminent rewind scenario, result_state completion scenario, level-select probe) all replayed deterministically: two fresh replays per trace matched every recorded state and rendered-pixel digest. Observed with real inputs: title flow, chapter menu with four chapters, level select with six level buttons, 30 s HUD countdown with timeline bar and Reset button, movement via held keys, R-reset clearing all ghost tracks, ESCAPE pause overlay freezing the sim, a scheduled rewind (loop 2->3) after which replaying ghosts hold plate_1 (Switches Held 1/1), and a four-ghost preloaded state where plates, door and laser are held/blocked and the Level Complete panel shows Loops Used: 2 and Time in Final Loop: 10.00 s. Recorded visible defects: literal 'Chapter %d' level-select header, a rewind flash overlay that never fades (frame 599 fully washed out, flash_timer stuck at 0.35), second ESCAPE not unpausing, stray clipped sprite at top-left in scenario start frames, and several dialog/HUD placement issues. evidence_mappings.rationale: Ordinary fresh launch frame 0 pixels show the TIME LOOP title over overlapping clock hands with ghost silhouettes at lower left/right, plus Chapter Menu and Quick Start buttons at their observed rects, evidencing the normal title flow.

After clicking the observed Chapter Menu rect, frame 119 shows the Chapters panel with exactly four chapter buttons (Chapter 1-4 rects [480,210..465,320x72]) and a Back button, matching the four-chapter menu requirement.

Frame 239 shows six level entries (Level 1-6 button rects in two columns) after selecting Chapter 1, evidencing the six-levels-per-chapter reveal; the header text defect is reported separately as a finding.

Frame 45 after Quick Start shows HUD 'Time: 29.20' counting down from 30, 'Loop 1', timeline bar node with max_time 30 at rect [36,58,1204,30], and the Reset button rect, evidencing countdown start and top timeline presence.
Player CharacterBody2D position moved from spawn [110,608] to [330,605.9] with facing_left true after the held RIGHT then LEFT inputs, evidencing run-left/right control response during ordinary play.

After the R key press at frame 300, frame 330 shows tracks [], ghost_sprites [], loop_count 1, loop_time 29.03 and player back at spawn [110,608], evidencing reset clearing all ghosts and restarting fresh.

Frame 120 shows loop_count advanced 2->3, loop_time reset to 29.03, sim_tick restarted at 29, flash_timer 0.35 and player returned to the spawn x=110, evidencing timer expiry triggering rewind and respawn with a flash trigger.

Frame 599 shows two ghost sprites replaying while the live player idles at spawn, plate_1 active true with 'Switches Held: 1 / 1' caused by a ghost standing on it, and timeline fractions with two ghost entries, evidencing simultaneous ghost world interaction and timeline ghost positions.

Frame 5 shows four ghost tracks holding all four required plates active, door_main open true, laser_main blocked true, and completed true with the player inside exit_rect, evidencing layered multi-loop contributions including laser blocking gating completion.

Frame 299 pixels and labels show the Level Complete panel displaying 'Loops Used: 2' and 'Time in Final Loop: 10.00 s' with Next Level / Retry Level / Chapter Menu buttons, evidencing the completion summary content.

limitations: Trial budget is zero; no further play, retry or replay is possible in this invocation.
Visual review was limited to the eight supplied screenshot pixels; all other frames are interpreted from structured node observations only.
The 600-frame (20 s) capture cap cannot show a full ordinary 30-second loop expiry from a normal level start; the loop_rewrite_imminent scenario was used for the rewind transition.
result_state is a preloaded completion state and is not proof of ordinary menu-to-exit completion.
No packaged demo_outputs/*.json traces were present in the supplied data, so replay of shipped demos remains pending.
Airborne jump state, ENTER lever interaction and ordinary-play exit completion were not captured; their absence here is not evidence of failure.
Findings are Player interpretations, not QA verdicts; requirement verification remains with QA.
This is a custom public trace harness, not the hidden official evaluator or a QA verdict.
Determinism means matching bounded observed state and rendered pixels at every recorded frame on this fixed engine/image; hidden state, other seeds and other platforms are not proved.
Selected capture screenshots were supplied as image input. Unseen scenes and frames are not visually verified.
Godot wall-clock time is not rewritten; wall-clock animations can legitimately fail exact visual replay.
